sentences.text: Adelolophus is a genus of crested duck-bill dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Utah, and it is the only known species of this extinct ornithischian hadrosaur genus.
The only known specimen is a broken upper jawbone, specifically a maxilla, whose anatomy identifies it as a lambeosaurine dinosaur.
The triangular shape of this single bone identifies it as a lambeosaur, a type of dinosaur with large hollow head crests, featuring a large, elevated triangular process near the back of the jawbone.
It possesses a unique, thickened ridge running from the jaw joint to the palatine process, a feature not seen in other lambeosaurs, which distinguishes the genus despite its fragmentary nature.
The genus name means "unknown crest" because the fossil does not show the crest that is typical for its relatives.
Researchers interpreted Adelolophus as the oldest known lambeosaurine in North America, dating to approximately 78 million years ago.
Adelolophus was described by Terry Gates and colleagues in 2014, after the maxilla was first reported in a scientific article by the same team in 2013.
John Howard Hutchison and colleagues collected fossils at the site in 1999 based on earlier reports by Howard D. Zeller, and the species name honors Dr. Howard Hutchison, who found the specimen.
It lived in a wet environment near the sea that experienced arid seasons, specifically a tidal estuary with meandering rivers and brackish water influenced by the Western Interior Seaway.

It shared its habitat with fish such as sturgeon, gar, and the large bowfin fish Melvius, as well as abundant turtles of the extinct baenid family, including Arvinachelys, Denazinemys, and Neurankylus.
It shared its habitat with the ceratopsid dinosaur Machairoceratops, which is also from the Upper Member.
Adelolophus belongs to the lambeosaurine subfamily of the Hadrosauridae family, and its parent group is Lambeosaurinae.
Phylogenetic analysis places it within the tribe Parasaurolophini, a finding supported by a 2021 study and subsequent research confirming its membership in this tribe.

It lived during the early Campanian age in the Upper Member of the Wahweap Formation, where the environment was tidal, characterized by meandering rivers that created an estuarine environment with brackish water.

Adelolophus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 77 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America, with a time range for the species being the Campanian, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
